title.narrative: Water Resources Management Sector Project (formerly Irrigation Project / Agriculture Sector Development)

description.narrative: The Project continues the support of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) for the rehabilitation and upgrading of irrigation and drainage infrastructure and capacity development for water management. The Project is structured as a sector loan project. It involves two areas of the country: (i) the Zarafshan River Basin, and (ii) the Fergana Valley. The Project will (i) rehabilitate and upgrade pumping stations, (ii) rehabilitate and upgrade inter-farm irrigation and drainage canals and structures, and (iii) improve inter-farm water management through state water agencies and on-farm management through water users' associations (WUAs). The primary aim is sustained and increased agriculture productivity.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Irrigation systems fully functional and operated in an efficient manner.

20% improvement in energy efficiency Progress/Status: Achieved. The efficiency of the old pumping units was estimated to vary from 45% of Besharyk to 75% of Dangara with average of 56.1%. The average efficiency of the new units is 83.8%, thus an increase of 27.7%. Data Source: Provincial and district statistics. Project performance monitoring and reports by the PMO. Base year: 2014 Baseline value: N

Area irrigated in the subprojects does not fall below the average of the last 3 years Progress/Status: Achieved. While the command areas of the subprojects remained the same, the irrigated area increased from 63,177 ha at appraisal to 70,830 ha at project completion, i.e. an increase of 12.1%. Data Source: Provincial and district statistics. Project performance monitoring and reports by the PMO. Base year: 2014 Baseline value: N

Water conveyance losses reduced by 10% Progress/Status: Achieved. With the improvement of the inter-farm canals, the conveyance efficiency in the subprojects is estimated to have increased from 60-70% to 90%, an increase of 20-30%. Data Source: Provincial and district statistics. Project performance monitoring and reports by the PMO. Base year: 2014 Baseline value: N

Output: 2. Improved water management capacity Indicator: 100% coverage of subproject command area by trained WUAs Progress/Status: Achieved. Following the agreement during the Inception Mission, the scope of WCA was expanded to the areas of the districts of the subprojects rather than the command areas of the subprojects. Thus, the existing 38 WCAs were reorganized on hydrographic boundaries and registered as nonprofit WCAs. As a result, 34 WCAs were established compared to 20 WCAs envisages in the PIP. They cover 100% command area of all subprojects. The WCAs were fully trained in all relevant aspects. Data Source: Project performance monitoring and reports of the PMO. Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 2. Improved water management capacity Indicator: All WUAs monitor water distribution and have water on-farm water management plans in place Progress/Status: Achieved. With intensive on-the-job training and regular coaching, the WCAs were able to prepare the required on-farm water management plans and monitor their implementation. Data Source: Project performance monitoring and reports of the PMO. Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 2. Improved water management capacity Indicator: Capacity development program implemented for improved water management of interfarm infrastructure Progress/Status: Achieved. A capacity development program for improved water management of inter-farm infrastructure was prepared after a thorough assessment of the existing situation and potential for improvement of water resources management organizations in the project area. The program was implemented by June 2015. Data Source: BISA and other water authority records. Project performance monitoring and reports of the PMO. Guidelines and proposals on development of water use schedules and O&M of irrigation systems were prepared using Narpay subproject as a case study. These were presented in the Guidelines and Proposals for Operation, Maintenance, and Water Management Planning for Integrated and Coordinated Operation of Inter-farm and On-farm Infrastructure with Case Study of Narpay Irrigation Subproject, developed by SDC's consultant under the project.
